characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 0.02Nb steel consists of ferrite (δ) and austenite (γ).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apollo 300 thermal field emission SEM equipped with EBSD detector
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregular ferrite dispersed in austenite matrix; austenite grain size 18 μm and ferrite grain size 3.6 μm in the as-cast 0.02Nb steel.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD step size 300 nm; electropolished with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol solution at 25 V for 10 s before observation
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure characterization and grain size measurement

characterization_methods.key_findings: Nb uniformly dispersed in austenite with sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries; austenite composition (wt%): Mn 13.12, Al 8.35, Cr 4.06, C 1.39, Nb 0.019, Fe 63.79.
characterization_methods.purpose: elemental distribution analysis; austenite matrix composition

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JEM-2100 TEM (200 kV); double-jet electropolishing with 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol at ≈30 °C and 35 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: Submicron white particles identified as NbC (Spot 1, SAED [100]γ//[100]NbC); nano-scale κ-carbides with size 2.0 nm and volume fraction 3.3 vol% in the as-cast state, coherent [100]γ//[100]κ.
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation load 200 gf; holding time 20 s

characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 0.02Nb steel: yield strength 880 ± 19 MPa, tensile strength 1016 ± 12 MPa, total elongation 39 ± 2 %.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature; strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; gauge width 4 mm; gauge length 12 mm; minimum four repetitions

analytical_models.equation_role: calculate formation energy of κ-carbide structures (undoped and Nb-doped)
analytical_models.model_name: formation energy equation E_F = E_DFT − Σ N_X μ_X
analytical_models.model_note: Nb doping increases κ-carbide formation energy; lower E_F indicates greater stability.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 2×2×2 supercell of κ-carbide (Fe3AlC, E21); plane-wave cutoff 500 eV; Gaussian smearing 0.05 eV; energy convergence <0.03 eV Å^-1; vacuum spacing 15 Å; 6×6×6 Monkhorst-Pack k-points
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Projector augmented wave (PAW) potentials; U scheme 2.59 eV for Fe atoms
computational_details.simulation_method: Spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) within generalized gradient approximation (GGA), PBE recipe

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: temperature range 673–873 K; diffusing species Al and C in austenite of 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels

analytical_models.model_name: Hall-Petch grain boundary strengthening (σg = k_γ d^-1/2)
Taylor dislocation strengthening (σd = M α G b √ρ)

analytical_models.equation_role: calculate κ-carbide precipitation strengthening in austenite
analytical_models.model_name: κ-carbide shearing precipitation strengthening (σp = (M/N)(γ_APB/b)√Vf[√(12γ_APB r/(π G b^2)) − √Vf])
analytical_models.model_note: The paper text renders the antiphase boundary energy unit as 'm m^-2' (garbled); value kept as reported.

analytical_models.model_name: Ashby-Orowan strengthening for NbC particles (σoro = (0.538 G b f^1/2 / D) × ln(D/2b))
analytical_models.model_note: Based on NbC content f and average size D from Figure 4.
Ferrite dislocation density from Table 8 (ρ = 9.69 × 10^14 m^-2 for as-cast 0.02Nb).

computational_details.simulation_method: Quantitative analytical strengthening analysis of austenite and ferrite

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: NbC particles can pin austenite grain boundary motion during δ-ferrite → γ-austenite transformation, hindering austenite grain growth.

interfaces.phase_evolution: retention of metastable austenite at room temperature through near-rapid solidification and subsequent cooling

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength improvement ≈71 MPa (0.04Nb steels vs 0.02Nb steels overall)

processing_steps.method: induction melting in water-cooled copper crucible
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Initial ingot preparation step before re-melting and casting.

processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification (re-melting and high-speed pouring into rotating copper mold)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Produces as-cast steel strips with dimensions 60 × 70 × 2.5 mm; no subsequent aging treatment for the as-cast sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: minimum of four repetitions per steel strip
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: As-cast (black) curve extends to roughly 38% strain at a plateau of ~1000–1050 MPa (Figure 9a).

phases_present.morphology: austenite matrix; equiaxed polygonal austenite grains
irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix

precipitates.distribution: sparse submicron white particles within the austenite matrix; volume fraction near 0 vol% in the as-cast state (read from Figure 4)
nano-scale κ-carbides dispersed in austenite; volume fraction 3.3 vol% in the as-cast state

structures.overall_structure: irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix; microstructure consists of ferrite and austenite
